title: Ibuka
summary: Rwanda's history, made to be moved through.

sections.body:
**Our history, for people who weren't there.**

I wanted younger generations to be able to see our history unfold, rather than only reading about it in textbooks.

sections.heading: How it's told
sections.body:
Ibuka is an interactive narrative you navigate with sound, moving through each scene at your own pace.

It doesn't begin in 1994. It begins with a colonial border drawn across a map, and with these words: *Before the cards. Before the labels. There were neighbors.*

From there, it journeys through five chapters from the colonial era to the present day.
sections.caption: The opening scene.

sections.heading: How it ends
sections.body:
The final chapter is called The Weavers.

It closes with survivors sitting alongside the wives of perpetrators, weaving traditional *agaseke* baskets together. The woven pattern is named "women holding hands".

sections.heading: The response
sections.body:
I created it for my peers.

Over 21,000 people visited during its launch week.

Nothing in it is gamified, and nothing is rushed.
